meta.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Expand a Sentence - Rhetorical Grammar
meta.title: Expand a Sentence: Rhetorical Grammar

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands 'The birds sang' by adding a fronted prepositional phrase?
choices: The birds, perched on the highest branch, sang.
The birds sang with great enthusiasm.
In the early morning, the birds sang.
Singing sweetly, the birds greeted the dawn.
questions.explanation: The correct answer places the prepositional phrase 'In the early morning' at the front of the sentence.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands "The committee approved the plan" by using the correlative conjunction "Not only … but also" to add a second verb phrase?
choices: If the data supported it, the committee approved the plan.
The committee approved the plan and funded the project.
The committee, which reviewed the data, approved the plan.
Not only did the committee approve the plan, but it also funded the project.
questions.explanation: The correct option uses the correlative pair to coordinate two verb phrases.
questions.skill: Correlative conjunction adding a second predicate

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands 'The runner crossed the finish line' by using asyndeton to list a series of actions without conjunctions?
choices: The runner, exhausted but triumphant, crossed the finish line.
The runner crossed the finish line and raised her arms and smiled at the crowd and accepted the medal.
The runner crossed the finish line, raised her arms, smiled at the crowd, accepted the medal.
After the race, the runner crossed the finish line.
questions.explanation: The sentence omits conjunctions between the final three verb phrases, creating an asyndetonic list.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands the plain sentence "The project cannot start" by adding a fronted conditional clause introduced by "Unless"?
choices: Unless the budget increases, the project cannot start.
If the budget increases, the project cannot start.
Because the budget increases, the project cannot start.
When the budget increases, the project cannot start.
questions.explanation: The correct sentence places an "Unless" clause at the front, creating a fronted conditional clause that expresses a necessary condition for the main clause.

questions.prompt: Which sentence adds a participial phrase to the plain sentence about a team celebrating, showing how the celebration happened?
choices: The team, shouting with joy, celebrated.
The team celebrated with joy.
The team, after the match, celebrated.
The team, because it won, celebrated.
questions.explanation: The participial phrase shouting with joy adds vivid detail by showing how the team celebrated.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands 'The engineer designed the bridge' by adding a series of participial phrases that elaborate on the design process?
choices: The engineer designed the bridge and the road and the tunnel.
The engineer, who had studied structural dynamics, designed the bridge.
It was the engineer who designed the bridge.
The engineer designed the bridge, calculating loads, selecting materials, and consulting experts.
questions.explanation: The sentence adds three participial phrases after the main clause to create a cumulative structure.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands The student opened the notebook by using an absolute phrase introduced by a noun and participle without a preposition?
choices: With her hands trembling, the student opened the notebook.
The student opened the notebook, and her hands trembled.
Her hands trembled while the student opened the notebook.
Her hands trembling, the student opened the notebook.
questions.explanation: Her hands trembling is an absolute phrase whose participle describes the student's hands and whose subject differs from the main subject.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands "The team will practice" by adding a fronted conditional clause?
choices: The team will practice if the weather clears.
If the weather clears, the team will practice.
To improve, the team will practice.
Not only will the team practice, but they will also review tape.
questions.explanation: The correct option places the conditional clause at the beginning of the sentence.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands 'The committee approved the proposal' by inserting a parenthetical dash-enclosed phrase that adds a concession?
choices: It was the committee that approved the proposal.
The committee, although facing strong opposition, approved the proposal.
The committee approved the proposal, which was controversial.
The committee—despite strong opposition—approved the proposal.
questions.explanation: The dashes set off the concessive phrase 'despite strong opposition' as a parenthetical interruption.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands 'The teacher explained the concept' by using an it‑cleft that emphasizes the manner adverbial?
choices: It was with great patience that the teacher explained the concept.
The teacher, who was very patient, explained the concept.
The teacher explained the concept, and she did so patiently.
With great patience, the teacher explained the concept.
questions.explanation: The correct answer forms an it‑cleft ('It was … that') to foreground the adverbial phrase 'with great patience'.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands 'The chef prepared the meal' by using polysyndeton to list multiple actions?
choices: The chef prepared the meal, chopped the vegetables, seared the meat, and plated the dish.
The chef prepared the meal and chopped the vegetables and seared the meat and plated the dish.
The chef, who had trained in Paris, prepared the meal.
It was the chef who prepared the meal.
questions.explanation: The sentence repeats the conjunction 'and' between each verb phrase to create a polysyndetonic effect.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses parataxis, joining three complete independent clauses with semicolons?
choices: We listened carefully and asked questions before revising our notes.
We listened carefully, we asked questions, and we revised our notes.
We listened carefully; we asked questions; we revised our notes.
After listening carefully, we asked questions and revised our notes.
questions.explanation: The semicolons join three independent clauses without conjunctions, which is the defining pattern of parataxis.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands The scientist explained the results by adding a nonrestrictive relative clause that gives extra information about the scientist?
choices: The scientist who had reviewed the data twice explained the results.
The scientist, who had reviewed the data twice, explained the results.
Before the team checked the notes, the scientist explained the results.
Explaining the results clearly, the scientist surprised the team.
questions.explanation: The clause who had reviewed the data twice is set off by commas and adds nonrestrictive information about the scientist.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands the plain sentence 'They found the missing keys' by using an it‑cleft that emphasizes the place?
choices: In the garden they found the missing keys.
They found the missing keys in the garden.
It was in the garden that they found the missing keys.
The missing keys were found by them in the garden.
questions.explanation: Option 0 uses an it‑cleft construction to foreground the locative adverbial 'in the garden'.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands 'The artist painted the mural' by using a colon to introduce a series of actions?
choices: The artist painted the mural, sketching the outline, mixing the colors, and applying the layers.
The artist painted the mural: sketched the outline, mixed the colors, and applied the layers.
The artist painted the mural; she sketched the outline, mixed the colors, and applied the layers.
The artist painted the mural, and then she sketched the outline, mixed the colors, and applied the layers.
questions.explanation: The correct answer uses a colon after the main clause to introduce a detailed list of sequential actions.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands We planted native trees by adding an infinitive phrase that expresses purpose?
choices: We planted native trees while the habitat was restored.
We planted native trees because we restored the habitat.
We planted native trees, restoring the habitat.
We planted native trees to restore the habitat.
questions.explanation: The infinitive phrase to restore the habitat expresses the purpose of planting the native trees.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands the plain sentence 'The scientist publishes the findings' by adding a fronted conditional clause?
choices: Publishing the findings, the scientist celebrated the result.
The scientist, who completed the study, publishes the findings.
If the peer review succeeds, the scientist publishes the findings.
The scientist publishes the findings; consequently, the community responds.
questions.explanation: Option A adds a fronted conditional clause ('If the peer review succeeds') before the main clause.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands 'I have never seen such a sight' by using inversion after a negative adverbial?
choices: I have not ever seen such a sight.
I have never seen such a sight before.
Such a sight I have never seen.
Never have I seen such a sight.
questions.explanation: The correct answer inverts the subject and auxiliary after the negative adverbial 'Never'.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands the plain sentence "The author revised the manuscript" by adding a fronted adverbial clause of reason introduced by "Since"?
choices: Because the data were inconclusive, the author revised the manuscript.
Since the data were inconclusive, the author revised the manuscript.
Although the data were inconclusive, the author revised the manuscript.
When the data were inconclusive, the author revised the manuscript.
questions.explanation: The correct sentence opens with a "Since" clause, a fronted adverbial clause of reason that explains why the author revised the manuscript.

questions.prompt: Which sentence reverses the subject and object of one clause to create chiasmus?
choices: The coach challenged the players, and the players challenged the coach.
The coach challenged the players, and the players answered the coach.
The coach challenged the players, while the players listened carefully.
The coach challenged the players, and then the coach praised them.
questions.explanation: The second clause reverses the subject and object of the first, creating the characteristic crosswise arrangement of chiasmus.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands 'The library opened its doors' by adding a fronted adverbial clause of cause?
choices: Because the funding arrived, the library opened its doors.
The library, which received new funding, opened its doors.
The library opened its doors, and the community celebrated.
Opening its doors, the library welcomed visitors.
questions.explanation: The correct answer adds a fronted adverbial clause of cause ('Because the funding arrived') to the base sentence.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands 'A solution exists for the problem' by using an expletive there construction?
choices: There is a solution for the problem.
A solution for the problem exists.
The problem has a solution.
A solution, which is effective, exists for the problem.
questions.explanation: The correct answer uses the expletive 'There' followed by a form of 'be' to introduce the subject.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands 'She read the book' by using an it-cleft that emphasizes the direct object?
choices: She read the book carefully.
It was the book that she read.
The book was read by her.
Reading the book, she learned a lot.
questions.explanation: The correct answer uses an it-cleft structure to focus on the object 'the book'.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands the plain sentence 'The athlete broke the record' by using an it‑cleft that emphasizes the time of the action?
choices: It was at the championship that the athlete broke the record.
The athlete, who trained for years, broke the record.
Breaking the record, the athlete raised her arms in triumph.
The athlete broke the record; therefore, she earned a medal.
questions.explanation: Option A forms an it‑cleft ('It was at the championship that …') placing the time phrase in focus.

questions.prompt: Which sentence turns the idea that delay is unacceptable into a rhetorical question that directly challenges the audience?
choices: We cannot delay our work any longer.
How quickly we are working!
Are we willing to delay our work any longer?
If we delay our work, we will face problems.
questions.explanation: This rhetorical question presents the audience with a direct challenge and gives the idea greater persuasive force.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands the plain sentence 'The decision surprised everyone' by using a noun clause as the subject?
choices: The committee's decision surprised everyone.
What the committee decided surprised everyone.
Everyone was surprised by the decision the committee made.
The decision that the committee made surprised everyone.
questions.explanation: Option 0 replaces the simple noun subject with a noun clause introduced by 'what'.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands the plain sentence 'The city built a new bridge' by adding a fronted perfect participial phrase?
choices: The city, which secured funding, built a new bridge.
Having completed the design, the city built a new bridge.
The city built a new bridge, a bridge that spans the river.
To improve traffic flow, the city built a new bridge.
questions.explanation: Option A begins with the perfect participial phrase 'Having completed the design,' which modifies the main clause.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands "She studied the material" by adding a fronted infinitive phrase of purpose?
choices: Because she wanted to master the concepts, she studied the material.
She studied the material to master the concepts.
To master the concepts, she studied the material.
Not only did she study the material, but she also taught it.
questions.explanation: The correct option begins the sentence with an infinitive phrase that expresses purpose.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is periodic, placing the main clause after a series of introductory dependent clauses?
choices: After the debate, the chair declared the winner after the long delay and the final count.
After the debate, after the long delay, and after the final count, the chair declared the winner.
The chair declared the winner after the debate, the long delay, and the final count.
Although the debate was long, the chair declared the winner after the final count.
questions.explanation: The series of introductory dependent clauses delays the main clause until the end, making the sentence periodic.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands The researcher repeated the experiment by adding an adverbial clause of concession?
choices: Because the evidence was limited, the researcher repeated the experiment.
When the evidence was limited, the researcher repeated the experiment.
Although the evidence was limited, the researcher repeated the experiment.
If the evidence was limited, the researcher repeated the experiment.
questions.explanation: The although-clause expresses concession by showing that the experiment was repeated despite limited evidence.
questions.skill: Adding an adverbial clause of concession

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands 'The manager will approve the request' by using a correlative conjunction to add an alternative subject?
choices: The manager, along with the assistant, will approve the request.
The manager will approve the request soon.
Either the manager or the assistant will approve the request.
The request will be approved by the manager.
questions.explanation: The correct answer uses the correlative conjunction 'Either ... or' to join two possible subjects.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands "The manager approved the request" by using inversion after a fronted "Only after" phrase?
choices: The manager approved the request only after the review.
Only after the review did the manager approve the request.
After the review, the manager approved the request.
The manager, after the review, approved the request.
questions.explanation: The correct option triggers subject‑auxiliary inversion by placing "Only after the review" at the front.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands 'The teacher assigned the project' by using a pseudo-cleft to focus on the direct object?
choices: What the teacher assigned was the project.
The teacher assigned the project, the essay, and the presentation.
The project was assigned by the teacher.
The teacher assigned the project because it was due.
questions.explanation: The pseudo-cleft 'What the teacher assigned was the project' uses a nominal relative clause to highlight the object.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands The climbers stored their ropes by adding a prepositional phrase that tells where they stored them?
choices: The climbers stored their ropes inside the blue shelter.
The climbers stored their ropes before the storm arrived.
The climbers stored their ropes with careful teamwork.
The climbers stored their ropes after reaching the summit.
questions.explanation: The prepositional phrase inside the blue shelter tells where the climbers stored their ropes.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands the plain sentence 'The audience applauded' by adding a fronted adverbial clause of time?
choices: When the final note faded, the audience applauded.
The audience applauded when the final note faded.
The audience, after the final note faded, applauded.
Because the final note faded, the audience applauded.
questions.explanation: Option 0 opens the sentence with a subordinate clause indicating the time of the applause.

questions.prompt: Which sentence adds an appositive to the plain sentence about Ms. Ortiz explaining the strategy, and the appositive renames Ms. Ortiz?
choices: Ms. Ortiz, who is our new coach explained the strategy.
Our new coach, Ms. Ortiz explained the strategy.
Ms. Ortiz explained the strategy, our new coach.
Ms. Ortiz, our new coach, explained the strategy.
questions.explanation: The appositive our new coach renames Ms. Ortiz and adds information without creating a separate sentence.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands 'The runner crossed the finish line' by adding a resumptive modifier that repeats the noun?
choices: The runner crossed the finish line, dreaming of it for years.
The runner crossed the finish line, which she had dreamed of for years.
The runner crossed the finish line; she had dreamed of it for years.
The runner crossed the finish line, a finish line she had dreamed of for years.
questions.explanation: The correct answer repeats the noun 'finish line' in a resumptive modifier that elaborates on it.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands the plain sentence 'The committee approved the proposal' by adding an absolute phrase introduced by a noun and a past participle?
choices: The committee approved the proposal and funded the project.
The committee, despite strong opposition, approved the proposal.
Because the data were convincing, the committee approved the proposal.
The proposal approved, the committee celebrated.
questions.explanation: Option A uses the absolute phrase 'The proposal approved' (noun + past participle) at the start of the sentence.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a compound-complex sentence with two independent clauses and a dependent when-clause?
choices: When practice improves, confidence grows because the team performs better.
When practice improves, confidence grows, and the team performs better.
Although practice improves, confidence grows, and the team performs better.
If practice improves, confidence grows and the team performs better.
questions.explanation: The when-clause is dependent, while confidence grows and the team performs better are two coordinated independent clauses.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands the idea that the group will succeed by using parallel structure in which three verbs share the same grammatical form?
choices: We will plan, preparing, and succeed.
We will plan, prepare, and succeed.
We will plan, preparation, and succeed.
We will plan, to prepare, and succeed.
questions.explanation: The three infinitives plan, prepare, and succeed share the same grammatical form and create parallel structure.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands 'The engineer designed the bridge' by creating a cumulative sentence that adds successive modifying phrases?
choices: The engineer designed the bridge, calculating loads, selecting materials, and testing models.
The engineer designed the bridge, a sleek arch spanning the river, using recycled steel, and incorporating seismic dampers.
The engineer designed the bridge; it is a sleek arch spanning the river.
The engineer designed the bridge and built a sleek arch spanning the river.
questions.explanation: The correct answer builds a cumulative sentence, layering appositive and participial phrases after the main clause.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands the plain sentence 'That the project succeeds is important' by using an expletive it construction?
choices: It is important that the project succeeds.
The project’s success is important.
Important is the fact that the project succeeds.
That the project succeeds remains important.
questions.explanation: Option 0 introduces the dummy subject 'it' and extraposes the clause 'that the project succeeds' to the end of the sentence.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands the plain sentence 'The dancer entered the stage' by adding a fronted participial phrase that describes how she entered?
choices: Because she was spinning gracefully, the dancer entered the stage.
The dancer entered the stage, spinning gracefully.
The dancer, who was spinning gracefully, entered the stage.
Spinning gracefully, the dancer entered the stage.
questions.explanation: Option 0 places a present‑participle phrase at the front of the sentence, modifying the subject before the main verb.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands the plain sentence 'She loves the sunrise' by creating an antithesis with a contrasting clause?
choices: Because she loves the sunrise, she wakes early.
She loves the sunrise, and she watches it each morning.
Loving the sunrise, she greets each day.
She loves the sunrise; he prefers the sunset.
questions.explanation: Option 0 pairs the original clause with a parallel clause that presents the opposite preference, forming an antithesis.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands "The manager approved the request" by linking a second independent clause with a semicolon and a conjunctive adverb?
choices: The manager approved the request; consequently, the project moved forward.
The manager approved the request, and the project moved forward.
Because the manager approved the request, the project moved forward.
The manager approved the request—an unexpected decision.
questions.explanation: The correct option joins two independent clauses with a semicolon and the conjunctive adverb "consequently."

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands the plain sentence 'The engineer tested the prototype' by adding a resumptive modifier that repeats the noun 'test'?
choices: The engineer tested the prototype; consequently, the design was altered.
The engineer, after reviewing the data, tested the prototype.
Testing the prototype, the engineer discovered the flaw.
The engineer tested the prototype, a test that revealed the flaw.
questions.explanation: Option A adds the resumptive modifier 'a test that revealed the flaw,' which repeats the noun 'test'.

questions.prompt: Which sentence adds a restrictive relative clause to identify which students improved most?
choices: The students improved most, and they practice daily.
The students, who practice daily, improved most.
The students who practice daily improved most.
The students improved most because they practice daily.
questions.explanation: The clause who practice daily is a restrictive relative clause because it identifies which students improved most.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands the plain sentence 'The author revised the manuscript' by using an it‑cleft that emphasizes the reason for the action?
choices: Revising the manuscript, the author improved its clarity.
The author, who wanted a clearer text, revised the manuscript.
It was because the editor requested changes that the author revised the manuscript.
The author revised the manuscript; consequently, the publisher accepted it.
questions.explanation: Option A creates an it‑cleft ('It was because … that …') that foregrounds the reason.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands The course develops useful skills by using two balanced, parallel independent clauses?
choices: The course builds strong readers, and it creates confident writers.
Although the course builds strong readers, it creates confident writers.
Building strong readers, the course creates confident writers.
Because the course builds strong readers, confident writers emerge.
questions.explanation: The two independent clauses use matching subject-verb-object structures, with builds and creates expressing the parallel actions.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expands 'The committee approved the proposal' by using a correlative conjunction to add a second subject?
choices: The committee approved the proposal, and the board did too.
The committee, as well as the board, approved the proposal.
Both the committee and the board approved the proposal.
The committee approved the proposal; the board approved it as well.
questions.explanation: The correct answer employs the correlative conjunction 'Both … and' to join two subjects in a single expanded sentence.

feedback.correct: The hole swallows the batch and grows — your sentence expansion held its shape.
feedback.incorrect: The hole stays the same size. Reread how the structure signals its effect, then try again.
feedback.win: The whole map is swallowed. You can now stretch a plain sentence into whatever shape your purpose demands.
feedback.lose: The hole can no longer grow. Reset the round and review cumulative, periodic, and balanced structures.
